blocks.content: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.

rows: No security of tenure (holds office during President's pleasure)
Has security of tenure for a 5-year term
Direct removal by the President without parliamentary procedure
Impeachment process passed by both Houses of Parliament

items: Article 156 explicitly states that the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President and lacks security of tenure.
Unlike the President, there is no requirement for an impeachment process or parliamentary sanction to remove a Governor.
Questions frequently test the distinction between the tenure of the Governor (pleasure of the President) and judges or the CAG (fixed tenure/security of tenure).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governor holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
The term of five years is subject to the pleasure of the President, meaning the Governor can be removed at any time.
A Governor may resign at any time by writing under his hand addressed to the President.
The Constitution does not lay down any grounds or specific procedure for the removal of a Governor.
A Governor can continue to hold office beyond his term of five years until his successor enters upon his office.
